segments.arabic: [1005] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن امرأته فاطمة بنت المنذر عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر رضى الله تعالى عنهما أنها قالت
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his wife Fatimah bint al-Mundhir, from Asma’ bint Abi Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: أتيت عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها زوج النبي ﷺ حين خسفت الشمس فإذا الناس قيام يصلون وإذا هي قائمة تصلي فقلت: ما للناس فأشارت بيدها إلى السماء وقالت سبحان الله فقلت: آية فأشارت أي نعم قالت فقمت حتى تجلاني الغشي فجعلت أصب فوق رأسي الماء فلما انصرف رسول الله ﷺ حمد الله وأثنى عليه،
segments.english: I came to ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when the sun was eclipsed. The people were standing in prayer, and she was standing in prayer. I said: “What is happening with the people?” She pointed with her hand toward the sky and said: “Glory be to Allah.” I said: “A sign?” She indicated: yes. She said: I stood until faintness overcame me, and I began pouring water over my head. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished, he praised Allah and extolled Him.

segments.arabic: ثم قال: ما من شيء كنت لم أره إلا قد رأيته في مقامي هذا حتى الجنة والنار ولقد أوحي إلي أنكم تفتنون في القبور مثل أو قريبا من فتنة الدجال
segments.english: Then he said: “There is nothing I had not seen before but that I have seen it while standing here, even Paradise and the Fire. It has been revealed to me that you will be tested in the graves with a trial like, or close to, the trial of the Dajjal—

segments.arabic: لا أدري أيتهما قالت أسماء
segments.english: I do not know which of the two Asma’ said.

segments.arabic: يؤتى أحدكم فيقال له ما علمك بهذا الرجل فأما المؤمن أو الموقن
segments.english: one of you will be approached and asked: ‘What do you know of this man?’ As for the believer, or the one who is certain—

segments.arabic: لا أدري أي ذلك قالت أسماء
segments.english: I do not know which of those Asma’ said.

segments.arabic: فيقول محمد رسول الله ﷺ جاءنا بالبينات والهدى فأجبنا وآمنا واتبعنا فيقال له نم صالحا فقد علمنا إن كنت لموقنا وأما المنافق أو المرتاب
segments.english: he will say: ‘Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to us with clear proofs and guidance. We responded, believed and followed.’ It will be said to him: ‘Sleep in peace; we have known that you were indeed certain.’ As for the hypocrite, or the one who doubts—

segments.arabic: لا أدري أيتهما قالت أسماء
segments.english: I do not know which of the two Asma’ said.

segments.arabic: فيقول لا أدري سمعت الناس يقولون شيئا فقلته
segments.english: he will say: ‘I do not know. I heard people saying something, so I said it.’”

checkedBody: Asma' bint Al Bakr said, "I came to 'Aisha the wife of the Prophet (p.b.u.h) during the solar eclipse. The people were standing and offering the prayer and she was also praying too. I asked her, 'What has happened to the people?' She pointed out with her hand towards the sky and said, 'Subhan-Allah'. I said, 'Is there a sign?' She pointed out in the affirmative." Asma' further said, "I too then stood up for the prayer till I fainted and then poured water on my head. When Allah's Apostle had finished his prayer, he thanked and praised Allah and said, 'I have seen at this place of mine what I have never seen even Paradise and Hell. No doubt, it has been inspired to me that you will be put to trial in the graves like or nearly like the trial of (Masih) Ad-Dajjal. (I do not know which one of the two Asma' said.) (The angels) will come to everyone of you and will ask what do you know about this man (i.e. Muhammad). The believer or a firm believer (I do not know which word Asma' said) will reply, 'He is Muhammad, Allah's Apostle (p.b.u.h) who came to us with clear evidences and guidance, so we accepted his teachings, believed and followed him.' The angels will then say to him, 'Sleep peacefully as we knew surely that you were a firm believer.' The hypocrite or doubtful person (I do not know which word Asma' said) will say, 'I do not know. I heard the people saying something so I said it (the same).' "
comparisons.note: The pinned body misspells Asma bint Abi Bakr. It also supplies explanatory angels and identity glosses absent from the selected Arabic. The exact source chain and all narrator-uncertainty comments are retained; the damaged comparison is not used as narration wording.

notes: The full chain includes Hisham transmitting from his wife Fatimah bint al-Mundhir, followed by Asma bint Abi Bakr. The companion honorifics retain Most High and the distinction between both persons and her. The pinned Khan body misspells Asma’s father as Al Bakr; this is disclosed as damaged comparison wording.

All three narrator uncertainty pairs remain in their source order. Each I do not know which Asma said interruption is a transmission note, not speech attributed to the Prophet. No named speaker is supplied for these comments. The first interruption follows the complete Dajjal phrase, unlike the placement in the separate selected report 86.

Faintness overcame me renders al-ghashy without asserting complete loss of consciousness. Ibn Hajar discusses this wording in the related Asma account. Neither a cause nor a legal ruling is inserted into the hadith. The hand gesture is retained where stated; a head gesture from the parallel occurrence is not added.

Sleep in peace is a provisional rendering of nam salihan. The two English comparisons differ here; Ibn al-Mulaqqin discusses the reassurance conveyed by the phrase. Detailed commentary stays outside the report, and independent lexical and theological review remains pending.

The selected passage names the Dajjal without adding Masih. The passive one of you will be approached does not name angels. No explanatory identification is added to this man. The three response verbs, all three Prophet honorifics, the final claim of certainty and the final doubter’s reply are retained.

Brill omits the opening companion honorifics and the Prophet honorific in the believer’s response, and supplies huwwa before Muhammad. The modern print has the shorter companion honorifics without Most High. The selected text is not silently harmonized to either print.

In the final reassurance Brill reads believer, while the selected source and modern print read certain. The working English retains certain; the two readings are not treated as identical. This difference was confirmed by magnified inspection of the complete closing passage.

segments.arabic: [1006] حدثنا ربيع بن يحيى قال: حدثنا زائدة عن هشام عن فاطمة عن أسماء قالت
segments.english: Rabi‘ ibn Yahya related to us. He said: Za’idah related to us, from Hisham, from Fatimah, from Asma’, who said:

segments.arabic: لقد أمر النبي ﷺ بالعتاقة في كسوف الشمس
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, indeed commanded the freeing of slaves during a solar eclipse.

notes: This brief report has its own full Rabi ibn Yahya route, source paragraph and chapter. It is not merged into the longer Asma account or treated as chapter material. The named narrators are not expanded with surnames taken from the adjacent report.

The emphatic opening is retained as indeed. Freeing slaves renders the historical term for manumission; no added recipients, legal conditions or modern commentary enter the report. Both prints preserve this separate occurrence; the Brill sentence crosses its page boundary.

segments.arabic: [1007] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك عن يحيى بن سعيد عن عمرة بنت عبد الرحمن عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها
segments.english: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Amrah bint ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

segments.arabic: أن يهودية جاءت تسألها فقالت أعاذك الله من عذاب القبر فسألت عائشة رسول الله ﷺ أيعذب الناس في قبورهم، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: عائذا بالله من ذلك
segments.english: A Jewish woman came to ask her, and said: “May Allah protect you from the punishment of the grave.” ‘Aishah asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Are people punished in their graves?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I seek refuge in Allah from that.”

segments.arabic: ثم ركب رسول الله ﷺ ذات غداة مركبا فكسفت الشمس فرجع ضحى فمر رسول الله ﷺ بين ظهراني الحجر ثم قام فصلى وقام الناس وراءه
segments.english: Then one morning the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went riding, and the sun was eclipsed. He returned in the forenoon. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed among the chambers. Then he stood and prayed, and the people stood behind him.

segments.arabic: فقام قياما طويلا ثم ركع ركوعا طويلا ثم رفع فقام قياما طويلا وهو دون القيام الأول ثم ركع ركوعا طويلا وهو دون الركوع الأول ثم رفع فسجد سجودا طويلا ثم قام فقام قياما طويلا وهو دون القيام الأول ثم ركع ركوعا طويلا وهو دون الركوع الأول ثم قام قياما طويلا وهو دون القيام الأول ثم ركع ركوعا طويلا وهو دون الركوع الأول ثم سجد وهو دون السجود الأول
segments.english: He stood for a long time, then bowed for a long time. Then he rose and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he rose and prostrated for a long time. Then he stood, and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he prostrated, but less than the first prostration.

segments.arabic: ثم انصرف، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ما شاء الله أن يقول ثم أمرهم أن يتعوذوا من عذاب القبر
segments.english: Then he finished, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said what Allah willed him to say. Then he instructed them to seek refuge from the punishment of the grave.

comparisons.note: The inspected web body shortens this four-bowing account to three bowings and omits the selected prostration comparisons. It is a limited comparison, not a complete rendering of this occurrence.

notes: Modern printed references 1055 and 1056 are both contained in the selected digital paragraph. The second continues the same chain. Both remain in full under app reference 1007; no missing-report suffix or new narrator is invented.

All four bowings, the long first prostration and the explicitly shorter later prostration remain. The Bewley web body omits the final standing and bowing and shortens the prostration details. The Khan body preserves this occurrence’s sequence; its explanatory affirmative-answer, journey, wives and sermon glosses are not imported.

This is not a copy of 1002: its opening chain, position of Aishah’s honorific, prayer verbs, prostration comparisons and final Messenger attribution differ. All five Prophet honorifics and the selected Most High companion honorific remain. Both readings and full scripts stay separate.

Brill places a shorter Aishah honorific at her question rather than in the opening chain; the modern print places it in the chain without Most High. The selected singular Malik related-to-me verb and source-specific attribution are preserved.
The request, ride and chambers retain the same unexpanded wording policy as 1002. The reply seeks refuge in Allah without adding an affirmative answer to the question.

segments.arabic: [1008] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن إسماعيل قال: حدثني قيس عن أبي مسعود قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Isma‘il, who said: Qays related to me, from Abu Mas‘ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: الشمس والقمر لا ينكسفان لموت أحد ولا لحياته ولكنهما آيتان من آيات الله فإذا رأيتموهما فصلوا
segments.english: “The sun and the moon are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. They are, however, two of Allah’s signs. When you see them, pray.”

comparisons.note: The inspected web body repeats its 994 wording, omitting the selected life clause and adding stand. The different Arabic reports and their independent narrator chains must remain separate.

notes: The complete Musaddad, Yahya, Ismail, Qays and Abu Masud route is retained, including Qays related to me. Both death and life, the signs clause and the prayer instruction remain.

The Bewley web body is identical to its body for 994 even though the selected Arabic reports differ. It omits life and adds stand. That mismatch is explicitly registered and disclosed; identical English comparison bodies do not authorize merging Arabic entries. The Khan body and both prints retain this occurrence’s death-and-life wording.
The separate chapter introduction names five transmitters and carries its own companion honorific. It remains Arabic browsing context with English pending, outside the report and narration script.

segments.arabic: [1009] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد قال: حدثنا هشام أخبرنا معمر عن الزهري وهشام بن عروة عن عروة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri and Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from ‘Urwah, from ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: كسفت الشمس على عهد رسول الله ﷺ فقام النبي ﷺ فصلى بالناس فأطال القراءة ثم ركع فأطال الركوع ثم رفع رأسه فأطال القراءة وهي دون قراءته الأولى ثم ركع فأطال الركوع دون ركوعه الأول ثم رفع رأسه فسجد سجدتين ثم قام فصنع في الركعة الثانية مثل ذلك
segments.english: The sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood and led the people in prayer. He prolonged the recitation. Then he bowed and prolonged the bowing. Then he raised his head and prolonged the recitation, but it was less than his first recitation. Then he bowed and prolonged the bowing, but less than his first bowing. Then he raised his head and prostrated twice. Then he stood and did the like of that in the second rak‘ah.

segments.arabic: ثم قام، فقال إن الشمس والقمر لا يخسفان لموت أحد ولا لحياته ولكنهما آيتان من آيات الله يريهما عباده فإذا رأيتم ذلك فافزعوا إلى الصلاة
segments.english: Then he stood and said: “The sun and the moon are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. They are, however, two of Allah’s signs which He shows His servants. When you see that, hasten to prayer.”

notes: The chain retains both al-Zuhri and Hisham ibn Urwah before Urwah; neither route is dropped or rewritten as a new independent hadith. The selected companion honorific includes Most High; both prints have the shorter form.

The explicit two prostrations are retained. The second-rakah statement and the later standing before the address remain separate. The closing clause that Allah shows the signs to His servants is preserved.

This repeated account remains separate from the other eclipse-prayer occurrences. No extra recitation, bowing, prayer formula or birth gloss is supplied from those accounts or the English comparisons.

segments.arabic: [1010] حدثنا محمد بن العلاء قال: حدثنا أبو أسامة عن بريد بن عبد الله عن أبي بردة عن أبي موسى قال
segments.english: Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Burayd ibn ‘Abdullah, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said:

segments.arabic: خسفت الشمس فقام النبي ﷺ فزعا يخشى أن تكون الساعة فأتى المسجد فصلى بأطول قيام وركوع وسجود رأيته قط يفعله،
segments.english: The sun was eclipsed, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up in alarm, fearing that it might be the Hour. He came to the mosque and prayed with the longest standing, bowing and prostration I had ever seen him perform.

segments.arabic: وقال هذه الآيات التي يرسل الله لا تكون لموت أحد ولا لحياته ولكن { يخوف الله بها عباده } فإذا رأيتم شيئا من ذلك فافزعوا إلى ذكره ودعائه واستغفاره
segments.english: He said: “These signs which Allah sends do not occur because of anyone’s death or life, but {Allah makes His servants fear through them}. When you see anything of that, hasten to remember Him, supplicate to Him and seek His forgiveness.”

notes: The complete chain distinguishes Burayd ibn Abdullah from Abu Burdah and Abu Musa. The source retains alarm and the fear that it might be the Hour; no date or Day of Judgment parenthesis is added.

The three superlatives in the prayer description and all three concluding actions remain: remembrance, supplication and seeking forgiveness. The selected source’s braces around the divine-action clause are retained as source punctuation, without adding a verse reference or claiming a separately checked Quran quotation.

The selected Arabic has no divine epithet after Allah sends. Brill adds mighty and majestic there; that wording is not imported. The earlier intake warning to retain source epithets is not evidence for adding one to this selected paragraph.
The Ibn Abbas chapter introduction stays separate in Arabic, including its Most High and both-persons honorific. Its English remains pending and it does not become an additional narration sentence.
